result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer A gives clear, consistent rules. It sets clear space and a minimum size for both screen and print, says when to switch to the mark alone, and covers one-color screen printing well, including a minimum stroke width and checking with the printer. Answer B handles the avatar better, with a heavier small version of the mark and a check at 32 px. But it contradicts itself on proportions: it sets the mark at 2.4 times the cap height, then aligns the mark to cap height plus descender. It also has odd wording ('sentence-free caps') and adds side notes, such as the trademark search, that the request didn't ask for. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B sets clear space and gaps in units of x, the height of the middle book, so they scale with the artwork. It also gives an explicit minimum size below which only the mark is used, and handles the tote's screen-printing limits in detail, with a minimum stroke and gap size and a check with the printer. A has a nice touch in its heavier small version of the mark for the avatar, but it has internal inconsistencies: "sentence-free caps", and a cap-height-plus-descender alignment that contradicts its own 2.4× mark-to-name ratio. It also gives no general rule for when to drop the full lockup, and its trademark note wasn't asked for.
